answer: Some economies assign admission slots by public randomness beacon rather than letting identities arrive at will. Each round opens a narrow window where an address claims one slot, so a thousand wallets cannot activate at once; they queue. The attacker pays in elapsed rounds, not in cheap registrations: thousands of identities must spread over thousands of rounds, and every ripple of beacon output reorders the queue. An honest agent needs one slot per epoch. An unfilled slot leaves a hollow the ledger cannot backfill, so by dawn it holds a few dozen identities, bought in weeks of waiting.
